entities.summary: The Mahabat Khan Mosque, sometimes spelt Mohabbat Khan Mosque, is a 17th-century Mughal-era mosque in Peshawar, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. The mosque was built in 1630, and named after the Mughal governor of Peshawar, Mahabat Khān Kamboh. The mosque's white marble façade is considered to be one of Peshawar's most iconic sights.
